scenes.headline: The Path of Renunciation
visual: Giving up the world, or giving up the ego?
scenes.say: Chapter Five. The Path of Renunciation. What does it really mean to give things up?

scenes.headline: Which one is better?
visual: You praise knowledge, and you praise service
Tell me, definitely, which is better
Arjuna wants a single answer
scenes.say: Arjuna is still not satisfied. O Krishna, he says, you praise spiritual knowledge, and you also praise selfless service. Tell me definitely which of the two is better. Like many of us, he wants one simple rule.

scenes.verse: The Supreme Lord said: The path of Self-knowledge and the path of selfless service both lead to the supreme goal. But, of the two, selfless service is superior to Self-knowledge.
scenes.say: Krishna gives him an answer, with a twist. Verse two. The Supreme Lord said: The path of Self-knowledge and the path of selfless service both lead to the supreme goal. But, of the two, selfless service is superior to Self-knowledge.

scenes.verse: The ignorant — not the wise — consider the path of Self-knowledge (or renunciation) and the path of selfless service (Karma-yoga) as different from each other. The person who has truly mastered one, gets the benefits of both.
scenes.say: And he immediately adds that the two are not really rivals. Verse four. The ignorant — not the wise — consider the path of Self-knowledge (or renunciation) and the path of selfless service (Karma-yoga) as different from each other. The person who has truly mastered one, gets the benefits of both.

scenes.verse: One who does all work as an offering to the Lord — abandoning attachment to the results — remains untouched by Karmic reaction or sin as a lotus leaf never gets wet by water, while living in it.
scenes.say: Then comes one of the Gita's loveliest images. Verse ten. One who does all work as an offering to the Lord — abandoning attachment to the results — remains untouched by Karmic reaction or sin as a lotus leaf never gets wet by water, while living in it.

scenes.headline: "I do nothing at all"
visual: Seeing, hearing, eating, walking, breathing
The wise know the senses move among their objects
The Self watches; it is not the doer
scenes.say: The wise person, Krishna says, thinks: I do nothing at all. Seeing, hearing, touching, eating, walking, sleeping, breathing, they know it is only the senses moving among their objects. The Self watches. It is not the one who acts.

scenes.headline: The Lord does not make our choices
visual: God does not create the urge to act
Nor the sense of doership, nor its fruits
Ignorance veils knowledge, and people are deluded
scenes.say: Nor, Krishna says, does the Lord create anyone's urge to act, or their feeling of being the doer, or their attachment to the results. These all come from nature. The Lord does not take on anyone's good or evil deeds. Knowledge is simply covered by ignorance, and so people are deluded. And knowledge, like the sun, reveals what was always there.

scenes.verse: An enlightened person — by perceiving the Lord in all — looks at a learned and humble priest, an outcast, even a cow, an elephant, or a dog with an equal eye.
scenes.say: What does such a person see when they look at the world? Verse eighteen. An enlightened person — by perceiving the Lord in all — looks at a learned and humble priest, an outcast, even a cow, an elephant, or a dog with an equal eye.

scenes.verse: Sensual pleasures are, in truth, the source of misery, and have a beginning and an end. Therefore, the wise do not rejoice sensual pleasures.
scenes.say: And what do they make of pleasure? Verse twenty-two. Sensual pleasures are, in truth, the source of misery, and have a beginning and an end. Therefore, the wise do not rejoice sensual pleasures.

scenes.headline: Sitting in stillness
visual: Shut out the outside world
Eyes and mind between the eyebrows
Breath made even, free from desire, fear and anger
scenes.say: The chapter closes with a first sketch of meditation, which Chapter Six will paint in full. Shut out the outside world. Rest the eyes and the mind between the eyebrows. Make the breath even. Free from desire, fear and anger, knowing the Lord as the friend of all beings, the sage finds peace.

scenes.headline: Both Renunciation and Karma Yoga Lead to the Same Goal
visual: Renunciation and selfless action are not opposites
Two roads to one destination
Master one, and you gain the fruit of both
scenes.say: Lesson one. Both renunciation and Karma-yoga lead to the same goal. They are not opposites. They are two roads to one destination, and the wise see that whatever is reached by one is reached by the other.

scenes.headline: Karma Yoga Is the More Accessible Path
visual: Complete renunciation is hard to sustain
Doing your duty without attachment is practical
Karma-yoga is recommended for most
scenes.say: Lesson two. Karma-yoga is the more accessible path. Giving up all action is extremely difficult, and true renunciation is hard to reach without Karma-yoga first. Doing your duty while staying free from attachment is a path almost anyone can walk.

scenes.headline: Where renunciation really happens
visual: External renunciation | Internal renunciation
Leaving home and duties | Staying, without craving
Rejecting the world | Free from likes and dislikes
Can still be full of desire | Free in any setting
scenes.say: Lesson three. True renunciation is internal, not external. A real renunciant is not someone who has physically left the world. It is someone who neither craves nor hates anything, and is free from the pairs of opposites: pleasure and pain, success and failure.

scenes.headline: The Yogi Acts, But Is Never the Doer
visual: The body, senses and mind act
Nature moves through them
The Self knows: I do nothing at all
scenes.say: Lesson four. The yogi acts, but is never the doer. The enlightened person works through body, senses, mind and intellect, yet knows that it is nature moving through them, not the Self. Holding that conviction, they act fully and stay free.

scenes.headline: Offering All Actions to Brahman Removes Karmic Bondage
visual: Offer every action to the Divine
Let go of craving for results
Untouched, like a lotus leaf on water
scenes.say: Lesson five. Offering all actions to Brahman removes karmic bondage. Whoever dedicates every action to the Divine, without craving the result, is no more stained by sin than a lotus leaf is wet by the water it rests on.

scenes.headline: Selfless Action Purifies the Mind
visual: Karma-yoga purifies the mind
Act with body, mind and senses, without attachment
Purification is the point, not the reward
scenes.say: Lesson six. Selfless action purifies the mind. Karma-yogis act with body, mind, intellect and senses, without attachment, for one purpose: self-purification. The work polishes the one who does it.

scenes.headline: The Body Is a City of Nine Gates — The Self Is Its Master
visual: The body is a city of nine gates
The Self dwells there as its master
It neither acts nor makes others act
scenes.say: Lesson seven. The body is a city of nine gates, and the Self is its master. The embodied Self lives in this city, the body with its nine openings, at peace. It neither acts nor makes anything act. Nature runs the city. Knowing this is freedom.

scenes.headline: God Is Not the Author of Karma
visual: God does not create our doership
Nor our actions, nor their fruits
Our own nature does; ignorance veils the truth
scenes.say: Lesson eight. God is not the author of karma. The Lord does not create our sense of doership, our actions, or their results. Our own nature does that. God neither takes on our sins nor our merits. Ignorance covers knowledge, and that is why we suffer.

scenes.headline: Equal Vision Is the Mark of True Wisdom
visual: A scholar, an outcast, a cow, an elephant, a dog
The wise see the same Divine in all
Equal vision is the sign of wisdom
scenes.say: Lesson nine. Equal vision is the mark of true wisdom. The wise look at a learned priest, an outcast, a cow, an elephant and a dog, and see the same Divine in each. This equal vision, sama-darshana, is not a social theory. It is what wisdom sees.

scenes.headline: Sense Pleasures Are the Root of Suffering
visual: Pleasures of the senses begin and end
They are the womb of misery
The wise do not seek lasting joy there
scenes.say: Lesson ten. Sense pleasures are the root of suffering. Pleasures born from contact with the world have a beginning and an end, and they always leave a want behind. The wise enjoy what comes, but they do not look for lasting happiness there.

scenes.headline: Find Happiness Within, Not in the World
visual: Happy within, delighting within
Lit from within
That person reaches Brahman
scenes.say: Lesson eleven. Find happiness within, not in the world. The one whose joy is within, whose delight is within, whose light is within, reaches the Eternal. Circumstances outside can neither add to nor take away from that fullness.

scenes.headline: Master Desire and Anger Before Leaving the Body
visual: Desire and anger push us all
Master them while still in the body
That person is a yogi, and happy
scenes.say: Lesson twelve. Master desire and anger before leaving the body. Whoever can withstand the force of desire and anger here, in this life, is a yogi, and a happy person. These two impulses drive the cycle of suffering. Mastering them breaks it.

scenes.headline: Meditation, Self-Control, and Surrender Lead to Supreme Peace
visual: Senses withdrawn, gaze steady, breath even
Free from desire, fear and anger
Knowing God as the friend of all: peace
scenes.say: Lesson thirteen. Meditation, self-control and surrender lead to supreme peace. With the senses withdrawn, the gaze steady and the breath even, free from desire, fear and anger, and knowing God as the friend of all beings, the yogi attains peace.

scenes.headline: Renounce the craving, not the work
visual: Both paths lead to the same goal
Act like a lotus leaf on the water
See the same Divine in everyone
scenes.say: So, Chapter Five. Renunciation and action lead to the same place, and the easier road for most of us is selfless work. Renounce the craving, not the work. Act like a lotus leaf resting on water. See the same Divine in everyone. Next, Krishna teaches Arjuna how to sit, and how to still the mind.
